scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 4.0 (PMKVY 4.0) - including Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)
administering_body: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE); implemented via National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC), Sector Skill Councils and empanelled Training Partners
target_beneficiaries: Indian youth and school/college dropouts (broadly aged 15-45) seeking free short-term skill certification; experienced but uncertified workers via the RPL stream
support_offered_summary: Free Short Term Training (STT) in NSQF-aligned job roles with certification and placement assistance; Special Projects component for bespoke industry-specific training; Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) stream assesses and certifies experienced workers (reported across 200+ trades including construction, beauty, tailoring and agriculture) without requiring a full course, with a reported Rs 500 cash reward on clearing assessment and 3-year accidental insurance cover of Rs 2 lakh; PMKVY 4.0 phase runs approximately 2022-2026
eligibility_summary: Indian nationals with valid Aadhaar meeting the specific job role's eligibility criteria; RPL applicants must have prior work experience in the trade for which certification is sought
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (MSDE official site, PIB, MyScheme, YouthPower India, YuvaSathi)
notes: PMKVY 4.0, together with PM-NAPS and the Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) scheme, was folded into the composite Central Sector Scheme 'Skill India Programme' under a 2025 Union Cabinet restructuring (~Rs 8,800 crore combined outlay through FY2025-26, per PIB); confirm whether a PMKVY 5.0 or renamed successor exists post-FY26 via official MSDE notification. | [support_offered_summary]: RPL cash-reward and insurance figures are sourced from secondary aggregator sites (YuvaSathi, YouthPower India), not independently cross-checked against the primary PMKVY 4.0 guidelines PDF text in this session.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (PM-NAPS; formerly National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme, NAPS)
administering_body: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Directorate General of Training (DGT); implemented via Regional Directorates of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (RDSDE)
target_beneficiaries: Apprentices engaged under the Apprentices Act, 1961 (as amended 2014) in Central Government 'Designated Trades' and state-notified optional trades, and the establishments employing them
support_offered_summary: Government reimburses 25% of the prescribed stipend (capped at Rs 1,500 per apprentice per month) to employers via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT); reimbursement of basic training cost for apprentices who did not undergo formal trade training beforehand; in FY2024-25 the scheme reportedly engaged over 18 lakh apprentices across nearly 75,000 establishments, with more than Rs 3,200 crore in stipend reimbursement disbursed that year
eligibility_summary: Establishments (public/private) engaging apprentices in Central Government Designated Trades or state-notified optional trades under the Apprentices Act, 1961; apprentice minimum age and qualification vary by trade
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (Careers360, TMS, sarkariyojana.com, Uttarakhand Skill Development Dept portal, PIB)
notes: [official_website]: no dedicated central NAPS/PM-NAPS portal URL was returned in this session's searches; apprenticeship registration is widely referenced elsewhere as routed via an 'apprenticeshipindia.gov.in'-style portal but this was not independently confirmed here, so left as PENDING_VERIFICATION. | Renamed 'Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (PM-NAPS)' as part of the 2025 Cabinet restructuring folding it into the composite 'Skill India Programme' alongside PMKVY 4.0 and JSS; both 'NAPS' and 'PM-NAPS' terminology still circulate. A reported 30% stipend-hike recommendation was found but not confirmed as implemented/notified - treat any figure above the Rs 1,500/month cap as unverified.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)
administering_body: Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD), under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)
target_beneficiaries: Rural poor youth aged 15-35 (extended up to 45 for special/vulnerable groups including women, persons with disabilities, transgender persons, PVTGs, rehabilitated bonded labourers, trafficking survivors, manual scavengers and HIV-positive individuals)
support_offered_summary: Free residential skill training and placement-linked training across sectors such as retail, hospitality, construction and IT-ITeS; free boarding and lodging during training; benefit disbursement via digital voucher directly to the beneficiary's bank account; post-placement tracking and migration support for placed candidates
eligibility_summary: Member of a rural poor/BPL household aged 15-35 (extended to 45 for specified vulnerable categories); typically mobilised via Self-Help Group/Gram Panchayat/NRLM convergence structures
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (Wikipedia summary via search, apnaafatehpur.in, bharatmadad.com, projectsarthi.com)
notes: [official_website]: commonly cited elsewhere as a '.gov.in' domain but no exact URL was returned in this session's search results, so left as PENDING_VERIFICATION rather than asserted; recommend direct confirmation. Sources for this row are secondary/aggregator sites and a Wikipedia summary rather than a directly fetched MoRD circular (WebFetch to .gov.in domains is blocked in this environment), hence confidence held at the lower end of the Tier 2/3 band.

administering_body: Board of Apprenticeship Training (BOAT) / Board of Practical Training (BOPT), Ministry of Education
target_beneficiaries: Diploma holders, engineering/general graduates and vocational-stream students seeking Graduate, Technician and Technician (Vocational) Apprenticeship placements
support_offered_summary: One-year structured on-the-job training at PSUs and private establishments with a monthly stipend (sources report differing ranges, roughly Rs 3,542-12,300 depending on qualification/establishment and source); Certificate of Proficiency awarded on completion, registrable at employment exchanges as valid work experience; managed via the relaunched NATS 2.0 portal (launched 30 July 2024); a Lok Sabha reply dated 23 March 2026 cited 5,23,024 apprentices engaged under NATS during 2025 across all States/UTs
eligibility_summary: Engineering/diploma/degree graduates and notified vocational-stream students, generally within a specified window (commonly cited as up to 1-3 years) after completing their qualification
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (schemesinindia.in, Bajaj Finserv, alp.consulting, govtschemesindia.com)
notes: Distinct from NAPS/PM-NAPS: NATS (Ministry of Education/BOAT) targets diploma/degree graduates while NAPS/PM-NAPS (MSDE/DGT) targets ITI/trade apprentices; no evidence was found in this session's searches of the two schemes merging. | [support_offered_summary]: secondary sources report inconsistent stipend bands (e.g. Rs 3,542-9,000 vs Rs 6,800-12,300); exact current official stipend slabs should be confirmed directly against nats.education.gov.in.

administering_body: Government of Telangana; specific nodal administering department not confirmed in available sources
target_beneficiaries: Telangana youth and jobseekers seeking vocational skilling and employability training
support_offered_summary: Operates as Telangana's state skill development corporation (branded 'Telangana Skill Hub'), coordinating state-level vocational skilling and training delivery for Telangana youth; distinct from TASK (Telangana Academy for Skill and Knowledge), a separate IT&EC-department body focused primarily on engineering/degree-college student employability skilling
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (tssdc.in, NSDC state list page, Telangana IT&EC department page)
notes: [eligibility_summary]: not itemized in available sources within this session's search budget - left PENDING_VERIFICATION. | [support_offered_summary]: specific flagship programme names, course catalogue and current funding outlay could not be confirmed; only the corporation's identity, branding and general mandate were established from available search snippets. | [administering_body]: exact nodal department (e.g. Labour/IT&EC) not confirmed. | tssdc.in serves content over plain HTTP (not HTTPS), which may indicate an outdated or lightly-maintained portal; recommend verifying TSSDC remains the current, active Telangana state skill body (as opposed to having been superseded/absorbed by TASK or a restructured entity) before relying further on this row. Session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before a dedicated follow-up query on TSSDC could be run.

scheme_name: Andhra Pradesh State Skill Development Corporation (APSSDC)
administering_body: Government of Andhra Pradesh (established 2014 as the state's executive agency for skill development)
target_beneficiaries: Unemployed youth, ITI/polytechnic/engineering/degree students, school dropouts and women across Andhra Pradesh
support_offered_summary: Implements central schemes (e.g. PMKVY, ESDM skilling) alongside state flagship initiatives including the Naipunyam Andhra Pradesh scheme (formulated 2025, offering specialised training in AI, renewable energy and IT), a Deep-Tech Skilling Initiative launched in 2026 targeting 2 lakh learners in 2026-27 and scaling to 10 lakh over 5 years (quantum technologies, AI, cybersecurity, data analytics, entrepreneurship), CM Skill Excellence Centres, Employability Skill Centres (ESC) and Youth Training Centres (YTCs); operates the Naipunyam and Skill Universe portals with a stated ambition of 20 lakh jobs by 2030
eligibility_summary: Andhra Pradesh resident youth/students/jobseekers; specific age, education and income eligibility vary by individual programme (e.g. Naipunyam, Deep-Tech Skilling, ESC)
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (The Hans India, aimindia.in, tirupati.ap.gov.in district portal, CBInsights)
notes: [official_website]: commonly cited elsewhere as an 'apssdc.in'-style domain, but this exact domain was not returned as a confirmed link in this session's search results (only a district-level sub-portal, tirupati.ap.gov.in/apssdc, was confirmed) - left PENDING_VERIFICATION rather than asserted. | Figures for the Deep-Tech Skilling Initiative (2 lakh/10 lakh learner targets) and the '20 lakh jobs by 2030' goal are drawn from news/secondary aggregator coverage, not a primary APSSDC notification.

scheme_name: Tool Rooms & MSME Technology Centres Skill Training Scheme
administering_body: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MoMSME), Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME); delivered through a network of Tool Rooms and MSME Technology Centres (e.g. Central Tool Room & Training Centre Bhubaneswar and other Centrally Funded Technical Institutes) in public-private-partnership mode
target_beneficiaries: MSME entrepreneurs and employees, ITI/diploma/engineering pass-outs and industry personnel seeking tool & die-making, precision machining and advanced manufacturing skills
support_offered_summary: Long-term diploma-level training courses (e.g. tool & die making) and short-term skill-upgradation courses in machining, fitting, CAD/CAM, CNC machining, 3D printing, robotics and process automation; also provides tooling design/consultancy and testing services to MSMEs; aims to bridge skill gaps and build technical, managerial and entrepreneurial capability among target beneficiaries
eligibility_summary: Varies by course - long-term diploma courses typically require ITI/Class 10-12 completion; short-term upgradation courses are open to existing MSME workers, entrepreneurs and engineering/ITI students; specific admission criteria are set by each individual Tool Room/Technology Centre
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (dcmsme.gov.in course/scheme PDFs, Grainmart News, IndiaFilings)
notes: Distinct from PMEGP/CGTMSE (funding-focused instruments already catalogued in Package004) - this row covers the MSME Ministry's dedicated skill-training/technology-centre infrastructure (Tool Rooms and MSME Technology Centres), a genuinely separate skill-upgradation instrument. Course fee structures, specific stipends (if any) and the current course catalogue by individual Tool Room were not itemized with confidence in available sources.

administering_body: Ministry of Rural Development (funding), under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM); each RSETI is set up and operated by a Sponsor (Lead) Bank in its lead district
target_beneficiaries: Rural unemployed youth aged 18-45 with an aptitude for self-employment or wage employment
support_offered_summary: Free short-term residential skill-cum-entrepreneurship development training (minimum 6 days to maximum 6 weeks) across 73 NSQF-aligned courses spanning agriculture, manufacturing and services; free food and accommodation during training; post-training credit-linkage assistance from the sponsor bank to help trainees start micro-enterprises; approximately 590 RSETIs reported functioning across 572 districts in 33 States/UTs
eligibility_summary: Rural youth aged 18-45 with basic aptitude in the chosen trade; priority typically given to BPL/poor households; training provided free of separate application fee
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (rural.gov.in press release, PIB press release, DD India feature)
notes: [official_website]: no single dedicated national RSETI portal URL was confirmed in this session's searches (individual state RSETI/SRLM sites exist, e.g. jkbrseti.com, hsrlm.gov.in) - left PENDING_VERIFICATION rather than asserting an unconfirmed domain. Scale figures (590 RSETIs, 572 districts, 33 States/UTs, 73 courses) are drawn from a July 2026 DD India feature and PIB press releases (Tier 1/4 mix).

scheme_name: Skill Loan Scheme (IBA Model Scheme for Skill Development, NSDC-linked)
administering_body: Indian Banks' Association (IBA) model scheme, approved for implementation by member banks and other financial institutions as advised by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI); courses financed are typically affiliated with NSDC-approved Sector Skill Councils, State Skill Missions or State Skill Corporations
target_beneficiaries: Any Indian national securing admission in an NSQF-aligned skill/vocational course at an ITI, polytechnic, recognised school/college, or an NSDC/Sector-Skill-Council/State-Skill-Mission-affiliated training partner; no specific age restriction reported
support_offered_summary: Collateral-free loan reportedly ranging from Rs 5,000 up to Rs 1.5 lakh under the original IBA model (one secondary source cites this has since been increased to Rs 7.5 lakh - unconfirmed), covering course/exam fees and related costs; repayment period up to 3 years for loans up to Rs 50,000, with longer tenures available for higher loan amounts; no minimum course duration requirement, but the course itself must be NSQF-aligned
eligibility_summary: Admission secured in an eligible NSQF-aligned skill development course; available to Indian nationals through any IBA member bank or RBI-notified lending institution
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (Vajiram & Ravi, BankBazaar, National Skills Network, Indian Bank)
notes: [support_offered_summary]: loan-ceiling figures conflict across sources - most describe the ceiling as Rs 1.5 lakh, one (BankBazaar) states this has been 'increased to Rs 7.5 lakh'; the higher figure is unverified and should be checked against the current IBA model scheme document before use. | [official_website]: no single dedicated portal exists since the scheme is implemented bank-by-bank under an IBA model framework - left PENDING_VERIFICATION rather than citing one bank's page as canonical.

administering_body: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), implemented through a network of registered NGOs at the district level
target_beneficiaries: Non-literate, neo-literate and school-dropout youth and adults aged 15-45, with a strong focus on women, rural populations and other disadvantaged/marginalised communities
support_offered_summary: Community-based, non-formal, doorstep vocational training delivered with flexible schedules at low cost, in trades suited to local employment/livelihood needs; 294 JSSs reported operating across 26 States and 7 Union Territories; now administratively combined under the composite Central Sector Scheme 'Skill India Programme'
eligibility_summary: Age 15-45, with priority given to non-literate/neo-literate individuals, school dropouts, women and economically disadvantaged/marginalised community members; no formal minimum educational qualification required
notes: [official_website]: no dedicated JSS portal URL was confirmed in this session's search results - left PENDING_VERIFICATION. | JSS is now one of three components (with PMKVY 4.0 and PM-NAPS) folded into the composite 'Skill India Programme' Central Sector Scheme per a 2025 Cabinet restructuring with a combined ~Rs 8,800 crore outlay through FY2025-26 (per PIB press release).

administering_body: Directorate General of Training (DGT), Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE); delivered through a nationwide network of Government and Private Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) affiliated to the National Council for Vocational Training (NCVT)/National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET)
target_beneficiaries: School dropouts/pass-outs (typically Class 8, 10 or 12 depending on trade) aged 14 years and above seeking trade-specific vocational certification
support_offered_summary: Trade-specific training ranging from 6 months to 2 years across 169 NSQF-compliant trades, delivered via a network of 14,643 ITIs (3,331 government + 11,312 private) with approximately 26.58 lakh trainees enrolled; successful trainees receive a National Trade Certificate (NTC); DGT separately runs the Craft Instructor Training Scheme (CITS) to train ITI instructors, which NCVT has mandated for all ITI trainers
eligibility_summary: Minimum educational qualification varies by trade (commonly Class 8, 10 or 12 pass); minimum age generally 14 years, with upper age limits varying by state/ITI
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (DGT official site, National Skill Training Institute pages, Wikipedia summary via search)
notes: Scale figures (14,643 ITIs, 169 trades, 26.58 lakh enrolled) reflect the most recent figures surfaced in this session's search and should be periodically re-verified, as ITI counts change year to year.

scheme_name: Skills Strengthening for Industrial Value Enhancement (STRIVE)
administering_body: Directorate General of Training (DGT), Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE); World Bank-assisted (Program-for-Results financing)
target_beneficiaries: Government and private Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), Centrally Funded Institutes (CFIs) and Industry Clusters, with downstream benefit to ITI students, instructors and apprentices
support_offered_summary: Outcome-linked (Disbursement Linked Indicator-based) grants and technical support to improve the quality and industry-relevance of ITI training and apprenticeships, including gender-inclusion initiatives (reported female participation in ITIs/industry clusters rising from a baseline of 9.7% to 20.5%)
eligibility_summary: Selected Government/private ITIs, Centrally Funded Institutes and Industry Clusters meeting DGT/World Bank project criteria; not a direct-to-individual-trainee scheme
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (DGT official site, World Bank project page, Karnataka/Maharashtra state skill department pages)
notes: STRIVE was launched as a 5-year World Bank-assisted project with an original closing date of November 2022, extended by 18 months to May 2024; this session's searches found no confirmation of a further extension or successor project beyond May 2024, so this scheme's current (2026) operational status is unverified. Retained here as a real, distinct DGT/World Bank skill-quality-improvement instrument, but its active-vs-concluded status as of the collection date should be confirmed against dgt.gov.in before further use - do not assume it is currently accepting new ITI/cluster applicants.

scheme_name: SANKALP (Skill Acquisition and Knowledge Awareness for Livelihood Promotion)
administering_body: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), co-financed by a World Bank loan (reported at Rs 3,300 crore of a total outlay of approximately Rs 4,455 crore)
target_beneficiaries: State Skill Development Missions, District Skill Committees and training providers/institutions - an institutional/systems-level scheme rather than a direct-to-trainee stipend scheme - with indirect benefit to jobseekers via improved local skilling ecosystems
support_offered_summary: Institutional strengthening of skilling governance at Central, State and District levels; supports District Skill Development Plans and District Skill Training Calendars; quality-assurance and convergence support feeding into the National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) ecosystem
eligibility_summary: Institutional beneficiaries (State Skill Missions, District Skill Committees, training providers) rather than individual applicants
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (Drishti IAS, Insights on India, Delhi govt district portal, World Bank press release)
notes: A February 2026 Parliamentary Public Accounts Committee (PAC) review reportedly flagged planning gaps and slow implementation, noting only around 44% of the budgeted SANKALP provision was disbursed between 2017-18 and 2023-24; the scheme appears to remain formally active per a February 2026 World Bank press release referencing a related/successor skills-institute financing package, but the precise current relationship between 'SANKALP' as originally structured and this newer World Bank package is unresolved and should be verified. | [official_website]: no dedicated SANKALP portal URL was confirmed in this session's searches.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Dakshta Aur Kushalta Sampann Hitgrahi (PM-DAKSH) Yojana
administering_body: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (MSJE); implemented via the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC)
target_beneficiaries: Scheduled Castes (SC), Other Backward Classes (OBC), De-notified Tribes (DNTs), Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) and Safai Karamcharis/waste pickers
support_offered_summary: Short Term Training Programme, Up-Skilling/Reskilling, Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP) and Long Term Training Programme; reported monthly stipend of approximately Rs 1,000-3,000 during training; NSQF-aligned certification and placement support; scheme launched in FY2020-21
eligibility_summary: Applicant must belong to a specified target category (SC/OBC/DNT/EWS/Safai Karamchari), typically requiring a valid caste/income certificate
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment PDF, Drishti IAS, Sanskriti IAS, schemesinindia.in)
notes: A 2026 Lok Sabha reply reportedly found that fewer than half of PM-DAKSH trainees between 2021 and 2024 were successfully placed in jobs, raising post-training employment-linkage concerns flagged by Parliament; retained here as a genuine, distinct MSJE skill scheme, but placement-outcome effectiveness should be considered when profiling this scheme further.

scheme_name: Employment through Skills Training and Placement (EST&P) under DAY-NULM
administering_body: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Urban Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NULM)
target_beneficiaries: Occupationally vulnerable urban poor seeking self-employment or wage employment, with a minimum 30% women-beneficiary requirement and a 3% reservation for persons with disabilities
support_offered_summary: Skill development/upgradation training aligned to market demand to enable the urban poor to set up self-employment ventures or secure salaried employment; delivered via State/City Urban Livelihoods Missions and empanelled training providers
eligibility_summary: Identified urban poor individual (via city-level urban poverty/livelihood survey or Self-Help Group/Area Level Federation membership under DAY-NULM); at least 30% of beneficiaries must be women, with 3% reservation for differently-abled persons
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (Delhi State Urban Livelihoods Mission, FICSI, ASCI, NULM training module PDF)
notes: EST&P is one component of the broader DAY-NULM mission (which also includes Self-Employment Programme and Self-Help Group components thematically closer to entrepreneurship funding already covered in Package004) - this row specifically documents the skills-training-and-placement component to avoid duplication with that sibling package.
